reads.best: Large working system with dispatcher, SQLite kanban, dashboard and a big unit/e2e test suite.

reads.best: Substantial scoped storage, output validation, minimal child environments and recovery tests back its native Desktop media workflow.
reads.worst: The current product cannot delete saved takes or projects, music generation is unavailable, and local sound effects require separately configured engines.

reads.best: Paired clean controls, real-Hermes stub-model tests and lifecycle containment make agent safety measurable on the user’s own setup.
reads.worst: Known grading gaps can misclassify harmless payloads as failures or missed sends as resistance, undermining the central safety score.

reads.best: Integrates sandboxed live rendering, model import, GPU dry-run feedback and repair controls directly into Hermes chat.
reads.worst: No automated behavioral test suite is shipped for its sizable tool/backend; exported HTML runs model-written code without the Desktop sandbox CSP and loads a CDN at runtime.

reads.best: The workflow pairs evidence checks for personalized claims with cost disclosure, secret-store API access, code-bound human approval, and 213 focused tests.
reads.worst: The current PR text identifies v0.2.7 at a different SHA than this batch's v0.2.6 pin, so the reviewed tree is older than the PR description says.

reads.best: Moving credentials and human approval onto a phone is a strong, concrete trust-boundary design with closed action contracts and path controls.
reads.worst: The bridge is a powerful remote dependency and HTTPS is only recommended, so deployment security still depends heavily on the phone setup.

reads.best: The backend rejects stale targets and uncertain writes instead of replaying input, and integrates through Hermes's native provider contract ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbur0425/ownmachine/a93fbfec22281a01031a62629294e280fca4115b/plugin/ownmachine/provider.py)).
reads.worst: Apple Silicon, separate relay/guest/viewer provisioning, a custom Lume build, and in-process configuration make onboarding demanding, while model-driven pixel-click acceptance remains deferred ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rbur0425/ownmachine/a93fbfec22281a01031a62629294e280fca4115b/plugin/README.md)).

reads.best: Turns ordinary agent corrections into user-reviewed training data through lifecycle hooks, local scrubbing and usable export formats without automatically retraining a model.
reads.worst: The live _windows.open call omits session_key, so replies.py permits another direct chat on the same platform to settle the sole open card; its chat-isolation tests supply a key the live path never supplies.

reads.best: Automatic pre-turn recall and CJK-aware tokenization improve the agent itself while keeping notes local and human-readable.
reads.worst: Retrieval is lexical rather than semantic and bounded to Markdown, and indexing still scans file metadata during ongoing use.

reads.best: It improves Hermes's own approval system safely: 49 tests cover over-broad globs against Hermes's matching logic, an owner lock on gateways, and the rule that nothing is written without /habit accept.
reads.worst: README:61 promises it never proposes `docker kill`, but that is only excluded from glob forms; never_auto.py builds its strings 'from parts' so the security scanner skips the file; and config writes are not atomic.

reads.best: Measured live session shows 8 tool calls dropping to 1, with a dashboard tab and Desktop plugin.
reads.worst: Silently rewriting commands from learned lessons can misapply a fix in a different context; only four test files.

reads.best: By design it needs no broker account, API key, or network access at all, and is fail-closed and deterministic, with an ADR, architecture docs and ~780 lines of edge-case tests.
reads.worst: Because it only simulates paper trades against two mock adapters, it never actually touches a real brokerage, so its real-world usefulness is mostly as a policy-firewall pattern/demo rather than a deployable trading safeguard.

reads.best: A fresh human-ink-first contract: the agent can annotate and point at the user's own marks through vision-grounded tools but can never edit them, and each object keeps its provenance and can be replayed.
reads.worst: Setup needs three separate switches, the repo carries an archive of old engine versions, and it runs a local token-guarded web server that can be exposed past loopback.

reads.best: A large, finished dashboard with screenshots, about 13,000 lines of tests with recorded fixtures, no order or signing code, and its one optional key read only through Hermes's secret scope.
reads.worst: Node panels call the author's hosted relay (relay.perpdepth.com) by default, a third-party network call that is on unless the user turns it off, and the audience is a trading niche.

reads.best: A substantial pure layout engine, geometry tests, configurable shortcuts and illustrated UI make multi-session work much easier.
reads.worst: Its defining tiling features depend on the proposed upstream session-layout SDK; without that seam it falls back to ordinary tabs, with no manifest release floor.

reads.best: A real Desktop gallery and editor sharing one renderer with the FFmpeg exporter, with an SSRF-guarding proxy for browser capture and timeouts on every subprocess.
reads.worst: Heavy dependencies (Playwright, Chromium, FFmpeg) and the README itself says the v1.2 Desktop click-through is unverified and voice-over uses an internal Hermes TTS import.

reads.best: It adds a reusable safety boundary to Hermes across exchanges and trade-like tools, defaults to paper mode, fails closed on uncertainty and has strong pure-engine and integration tests.
reads.worst: It depends on adapters and Hermes approval-hook behavior, cannot see exchange-app actions, and its own README acknowledges MCP-hook coverage is untested.

reads.best: The implementation makes a serious attempt to fail closed across hooks and middleware, including durable limits and human-only live controls.
reads.worst: The pinned submission has no README and no tests, leaving a safety-critical integration hard to validate or operate.

reads.best: Native composer middleware and slots preserve the draft while attaching quotes to idle and busy sends, with focused behavioral tests.
reads.worst: Rejected-send recovery depends on a timed draft-text comparison, and the test runner needs manually supplied jsdom and nanostores dependencies.

reads.best: Proper memory-provider integration with prefetch recall, token-like statement refusal and scoped secrets; 42 tests and CI.
reads.worst: Depends on a third-party hosted service; README sparse on failure behavior.

reads.best: Tamper-evident memory that works with no configuration, with a minimal child environment and secrets fetched through get_secret.
reads.worst: The plugin folder has no README, and the Walrus side is a niche crypto storage service.

reads.best: Real machinery a prompt cannot hold: a pre_tool_call guard that stops other tools rewriting canonical story state, resumable runs, a cross-process lock and about 6,500 lines of tests.
reads.worst: It vendors 3.5 MB of an upstream project, including a minified prebuilt dashboard bundle, and pulls in fastapi, uvicorn and watchdog for a niche (mostly Chinese web-novel) audience.

reads.best: Polished product with pane, CI, browser and verifier tests.
reads.worst: Heavy local Node/Chromium/FFmpeg and npm downloads on first build for a niche creative workflow.

reads.best: Makes Hermes's existing usage records understandable through a native chart, breakdowns and read-only database aggregation.
reads.worst: Account rows reuse provider-wide usage and quota for every credential of that provider, so they do not establish per-account attribution.

reads.best: Uses Hermes-managed OAuth and secret store, read-only scope, and 12 real test files.
reads.worst: IMAP untested against real providers and the test tool advertises a deliver option it always refuses.

reads.best: Native delegation routing, bounded process supervision and a durable job fence address lifecycle and accidental replay rather than merely wrapping a prompt.
reads.worst: It requires a separately installed companion and vendor login, cannot relay vendor approval prompts, and does not enforce Hermes tool restrictions inside AGY.

reads.best: Makes real session and subagent work inspectable and adds guarded rewind through Hermes APIs with token and origin checks.
reads.worst: Multi-machine access carries session-control authority over plain HTTP, and rewinding conversation state cannot undo files already changed.

reads.best: It brings the user’s real browser to their Hermes agent, with isolated tab groups, extension-owned approval windows, revocable pairing and real-extension browser tests.
reads.worst: It imports aiohttp without declaring it, so a minimal install can fail to load, and its tailscale child inherits provider secrets; see [hub code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whoisdhana/hermes-chrome/b47cc7300bd4391cf125f5c9e4be50bb9e3475bb/hub.py) and [manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whoisdhana/hermes-chrome/b47cc7300bd4391cf125f5c9e4be50bb9e3475bb/plugin.yaml).

reads.best: Single-use expiring previews, revision checks, explicit confirmation and per-profile readback protect bulk model-setting edits.
reads.worst: It depends on private, version-sensitive host authentication and config APIs, supports only in-process local-file dashboards, and ships no automated tests.

reads.best: Dialect-aware rendering, scoped ElevenLabs secrets, session-aware stitching, explainable cue drops, and focused transport tests add real voice functionality.
reads.worst: Full cues work on text_to_speech calls rather than ordinary spoken replies or live voice mode, and the default backend requires a separate Fish Audio plugin.

reads.best: Addresses a widespread latency and token-cost problem with model-aware timers, persistent deadlines, savings accounting and targeted tests.
reads.worst: The pinned warm path reads agent.api_key and sends its own authenticated HTTP requests instead of Hermes credential routing, an explicitly unresolved admission blocker; it also depends heavily on private core APIs.

reads.best: A serious separation of agent and keys: a daemon enforces spend policy, the PIN is never a tool argument, receipts are signed and hash-chained, and about 600 offline tests run in CI.
reads.worst: Claims run ahead of the code: the manifest says nothing is signed until a human types a PIN, yet a handed-over sandbox pays any address without asking; keys and the signer password live in the plugin's own files rather than Hermes's secret store; and a download host is assembled from string pieces to get past Hermes's install scanner.

reads.best: Deterministic minor-unit accounting, source hashes, document verification gates, and extensive tests support cautious review.
reads.worst: The workflow serves a narrow agency use case and requires substantial manual staging and attestation of source records.

reads.best: Durable intake checkpoints and an explicit uncertain-delivery state preserve work and prevent blind notification resends after crashes [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/worker.py).
reads.worst: The pinned delivery and profile-binding paths still call private Hermes internals such as _live_adapter and _profile_runtime_scope, creating catalog-rule and compatibility problems despite substantial defensive logic [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kaosjammo/hermes-email-steward/a14b1c6ab76d23fb01e07a97b02990f6d4442273/email_steward/plugin.py).

reads.best: It gives existing profiles a shared terminal interface with bounded peer rounds, persistent completed messages and an explicit approval UI [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidpgil/hermes-stage/964c43b976124ea98b58a30cc8efbeb966d261fd/stage/entry.mjs).
reads.worst: Gateway readiness and RPC promises have no deadlines, and socket closure does not reject outstanding RPCs, so a dropped connection can leave startup or room actions waiting indefinitely [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/davidpgil/hermes-stage/964c43b976124ea98b58a30cc8efbeb966d261fd/stage/entry.mjs).

reads.best: Implements bounded HTTP, redirect and proxy refusal, secret-scope tokens, gateway restrictions, and detailed consent and failure-path tests.
reads.worst: Requires a separately hosted server and expiring full-account token, and agent save consent relies on a model-set boolean rather than an independent approval.

reads.best: The local deterministic engine uses configured argv, bounded execution, scoped fingerprints, and carefully states what a passing check does not establish.
reads.worst: The pinned README's install route points to a standalone archive missing from the fetched tree and says this is not a submitted entry; operators must resolve that packaging and entry-status contradiction.

reads.best: Credentials go only through Hermes's oauth/secret route, qbo_query is SELECT-only with clamped results, and setup docs are complete.
reads.worst: Setup still needs an Intuit developer app and manual refresh-token workaround, and date inputs are interpolated into queries unvalidated.

reads.best: WIRO_API_KEY is declared as a secret and handled only by Hermes, and CI runs integration tests against Hermes releases and main.
reads.worst: The capabilities are a hardcoded snapshot although the docstring says they come from the live catalog, and background tasks are billed from the wallet through a fixed paid model.

reads.best: Hooks into Hermes delegation and request middleware to shape model choice and effort, something a skill cannot do.
reads.worst: No tests at all for a non-trivial pricing/routing engine.

reads.best: Its pre-call interception, hard-limit rechecks, and post-call accounting give Hermes a reusable policy layer across tools ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmdry4530/hermes-guard-plugin/84c44e53ec43d3bac2c1a43d6a21aea0d58d4051/hooks.py)).
reads.worst: If policy evaluation fails and recording the fallback blocked-payment decision also fails, pre_tool_call returns None and permits execution instead of failing closed ([source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tmdry4530/hermes-guard-plugin/84c44e53ec43d3bac2c1a43d6a21aea0d58d4051/hooks.py)).

reads.best: User-only approval and drift revocation through Hermes file-safety and write_file dispatch.
reads.worst: No tests and a heavy, jargon-filled API for a review flow most users will not adopt.

reads.best: It solves a concrete stale-memory problem through a native pre_llm_call hook with per-call profile resolution and silence when nothing changed. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noprijbi99-dotcom/moment/1af58dda54a9ad9310acb4cad928a6db63f8403b/tools.py)
reads.worst: Shared state uses an unlocked read-modify-write with a fixed temporary filename, risking lost receipts during concurrent turns, and no regression tests are shipped at this pin. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/noprijbi99-dotcom/moment/1af58dda54a9ad9310acb4cad928a6db63f8403b/tools.py)

reads.best: It rejects invalid or expired quota readings, keeps multiple account pools separate, and labels remaining quota distinctly from used context [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aktogde1/hermes-usage-hud/097bbb5ef882dd6eb19d9afd9003e565130050e1/desktop/plugin.js).
reads.worst: Account reporting is hard-coded to openai-codex and its Session/Weekly windows, so users of other providers get no account-limit view [code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/aktogde1/hermes-usage-hud/097bbb5ef882dd6eb19d9afd9003e565130050e1/desktop/plugin.js).

reads.best: Code enforces contact cooldowns, cited scoring and draft checks, with focused safety tests and an offline demonstration.
reads.worst: Its draft-only guard relies on recognizing tool names and recipient text and returns no block on exceptions, so it is not a comprehensive sending boundary.

reads.best: Read-only store access, preserved failure history, cost reconciliation, rendered examples, and extensive privacy tests make the reporting useful and reviewable. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ryanomara/hermes-plugin-receipts/c7df9d35f6234eca9adeaa030e450b5ac8ea10e6/receipts/plugin.py)
reads.worst: Redaction remains pattern-based and requires manual review before sharing, while the README still uses placeholder repository install commands. [Source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ryanomara/hermes-plugin-receipts/c7df9d35f6234eca9adeaa030e450b5ac8ea10e6/README.md)

reads.best: The provider integrates native web search and host-managed OAuth, with clear setup, failure messages and local API-stub tests.
reads.worst: provider.py assumes results is a sliceable list of mappings and reads entire response bodies, so malformed or oversized upstream responses bypass its promised graceful-failure boundary.

reads.best: Scoped secrets, strict GitHub destinations, durable comment deduplication and tests for lost responses and rate limits give the queue a carefully engineered core.
reads.worst: Auto-claim examines only the first thirty open issues without pagination and claims are check-then-act, so busy queues can falsely appear empty and competing instances can claim the same issue ([service.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/krantikaridev/hermes-issue-orchestrator/9996a56a4dbdcf2bcd56f31f6940425b205af8da/service.py)).

reads.best: Careful backend: argv-only tmux calls, a strict pane-target whitelist, a fixed key set and no command-execution endpoint, with screenshots and a bilingual UI.
reads.worst: No tests at all, and it relies entirely on the dashboard's auth gate for routes that can send keystrokes and kill processes on the host.

reads.best: A real 3,600-line Desktop page plus an on_session_end index that tackles a genuine pain: hundreds of untitled Hermes sessions.
reads.worst: It reads the DeepSeek token straight from ~/.hermes/auth.json instead of the secret store, and cellar_rename/cellar_tag overwrite titles on the model's confirm=true with no human approval, unlike the README's 'only when you press Rename'.

reads.best: Careful confirm-before-upload flow, mandatory redaction, no token held, good tests and RELEASE notes.
reads.worst: Depends on ctx.redact_text and a hermes import flag that are not merged upstream, so by its own README it is not installable yet.

reads.best: Deterministic, no model call, atomic locked store with 18 tests, and an honest small A/B eval for its ask-before-deleting claim.
reads.worst: Crude regex keyword matching (one 'just do it' pins the level); a good system prompt or skill would get most of the effect.

reads.best: Prefers Hermes's own profile-scoped plugin_db storage API and a DEMO.md that explicitly lists 'claims to avoid' so contributors don't overstate it.
reads.worst: It is a fairly thin CRUD tool; nothing here (hooks, hardware, model/platform access) goes much beyond what a well-designed skill with persistent storage could approximate.

reads.best: The [Hermes tools](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasrobo/proofops/5916cc80d036a4ef81a961513ee973630393fcd4/__init__.py) expose PASS, FAIL, and NOT RUN with claimability and unverified items, making incomplete verification visible to the agent.
reads.worst: At the pin, [unset operator allowed_paths](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/rasrobo/proofops/5916cc80d036a4ef81a961513ee973630393fcd4/__init__.py) leaves filesystem roots to the model-written plan, allowing checks to read sensitive files outside Hermes's read guard.

reads.best: Deployment hooks distinguish blocking high-severity findings from medium findings that require Hermes's human approval. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oma035/Talos/f1485e33c951b0b4e5fb63a8fe7d55d8b7e183da/README.md)
reads.worst: Solidity scan-cache keys hash only the target file, so changes to imported code can leave cached deployment findings stale. [source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/oma035/Talos/f1485e33c951b0b4e5fb63a8fe7d55d8b7e183da/talos/scanner.py)

reads.best: Encodes real undocumented API traps as validation, dry-run and read-back verification.
reads.worst: No tests shipped and write access (analytics.edit) with niche audience.

reads.best: Honest README that discloses the side effects (posting, buying as you) and a known reconnect bug, with the key held in Hermes's secret config.
reads.worst: No local code and no approval gating: the server is not marked untrusted, yet its scripts can post or buy as the user, and the tool list is not in the pinned commit.

reads.best: A precise and unusual check for UI regressions, with screenshots at the boundary widths.
reads.worst: Windows/Edge only, needs a manual npm ci in the installed copy, and has no tests.

reads.best: Honest, small stdlib code with tests, timeouts, a non-blocking background probe and a README that says plainly it never switches providers or reads keys.
reads.worst: Despite the name it heals nothing: it only prints a reachability ranking, and 401/403 counts as reachable, so it overlaps Hermes's own fallback_model with less use.

reads.best: Polished README with banner, example and an honest account of what the watermark cannot do; useful for image provenance.
reads.worst: No code of its own: every call goes to a closed third-party remote server, and nothing is tested beyond manifest validation.

reads.best: Readable local retrieval code bounds excerpts and validates issued references, with synthetic-vault tests for scope and original-file preservation.
reads.worst: The native plugin registers only a skill; users must separately configure MCP, and its default scope file and cache live outside Hermes profiles.

reads.best: Read-only, no timers, extensively tested.
reads.worst: Useful only to CLIProxyAPI users; companion to another plugin.

reads.best: Deterministic exact-span quote checking with size limits is a concrete guard against fabricated citations that a prompt alone cannot enforce.
reads.worst: Three loosely related features glued from the author's other repos, covered by a single test in a shared multi-plugin test file, with a jargon-heavy README and no demo.

reads.best: Clear disclosure and a skill on scoping powerful tools for unattended jobs.
reads.worst: Mostly a vendor pointer: no code of its own besides a shell launcher, macOS only, needs a third-party app, no tests.

reads.best: Read-only by design: no executable code or stored credentials, OAuth through Hermes's own mcp login, and a skill that refuses money-moving requests.

reads.best: Uses Hermes secret config_schema and marks the server untrusted, with an honest README.

reads.best: Public job search needs no account and the documentation clearly discloses public profile data and application side effects.

reads.best: The package cleanly separates public catalog tools from token-gated account tools.

reads.best: Honest README with OAuth through Hermes and no stored credentials.
